scope: Bounded protected Standard_MMgrOpt::Initialize state reset on the actual optimized allocator; constructor shares the same path
source_capture_scope: 393 selected Standard/allocator/container sources, dependent test inputs, Cargo configuration and oracles; not a complete workspace compiler-input capture
behavior: MMgrOpt::new constructs zero initial storage, sets the requested parameters, and invokes the same actual initialize_native_free_lists method. No duplicate normalization implementation or detached graph was introduced.

Initialization preserves native operation order: correct page count, read system page size, disable mapping when page size is unavailable, compute free-list maximum, discard current free-list heads, round cell size. The clear flag, live handles, allocation headers, payload bytes, pool head, active cursor and pool end remain unchanged.

Recycled small blocks are forgotten by the actual free-list table without rewinding the active pool cursor. Allocation continues 24 bytes after the prior 16-byte block; subsequent Free and Allocate reestablish normal reuse.

Recycled medium blocks remain owned but unreachable from the reset free lists. Purge no longer releases them; new medium allocations do not reuse their still-live addresses. Live medium payloads remain intact, and newly freed replacements are purged normally.

Native Initialize takes no mutex and does not call or replace the process-wide allocation callback. Rust requires exclusive borrowing and leaves existing callback synchronization and Allocate/Free clearing paths unchanged. Native and Rust compare no Initialize event followed by one Allocate event.

Focused pool tests use the same legal protected page-size override in the native subclass and private Rust engine before allocating a real 6400-byte pool. Reinitialization restores the system page-size field while preserving that existing pool topology. Public adapter tests use normal constructor geometry and small medium allocations.

The native harness observes the discarded free-list array before freeing it, and cleans abandoned native medium storage only after comparison. A separate native-only fixture records calloc-table replacement and both old/new Linux descriptors remaining open, then explicitly closes them in the harness.
remaining_gaps_and_adaptations: Rust uses a sparse BTreeMap, not the native calloc pointer array. Native array allocation identity, byte consumption, old-array leak and unchecked calloc-failure state are not reproduced. The native-only table row remains uncredited.

The Rust mapping policy is a bool with anonymous OS mappings. Linux Initialize opens /dev/zero or /dev/null and retains old descriptors; descriptor identity, open failures and replacement/leak effects are not reproduced. The native-only descriptor row remains uncredited.

Rust retains ownership of abandoned medium backing until allocator drop; native forgets that storage and does not reclaim it on destruction. Heap resource-lifetime equivalence is not claimed. Safe invalid-handle refusal remains a Rust adaptation.

Native protected writable fields, arbitrary subclass operations and concurrent raw calls are not equivalent to the safe adapter. Exclusive Rust borrowing preserves safety; native Initialize itself provides no mutex protection.

Miri covers all eight new tests, ordinary Standard storage regressions, nine selected service memory tests and the original initialization-normalization test. The existing huge-pool stress was not rerun under Miri; every Standard service test, including all 19 pool/manager cases, passed normally.

As in the preceding shared-Standard-storage receipt, the service-memory Miri selection excludes the 1<<62 allocation case because it exhausts Miri compiler resources; complete normal tests include it. Unrelated locale FFI is outside this focused Miri selection.

The preexisting 167-record allocator reconciliation remains historical evidence from the prior candidate. This scoped binding adds evidence for one method without changing global inventory counts or claiming full allocator-family parity.
